about: What a state law that answers "raise the minimum wage?" with yes does to the state's rate when the bill names no dollar figure. ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: the size and pace of the real state increases from January 2013 to January 2024. A bill that files its own wage term (labor.minimumWage.hourlyCents) uses that term instead.
method: A run is a stretch of consecutive years in which a state's January 1 rate rose by $0.50 or more; its total is the rate at the end minus the rate before it began. totalMinor is the median run total; yearlyStepMinor is the median single-year rise of $0.50 or more. Ranges are the first and third quartiles. Indexed (cost-of-living) rises of $0.50 or more count with statutory ones: the table does not separate them.
source: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, Changes in Basic Minimum Wages in Non-Farm Employment Under State Law: Selected Years 1968 to 2024, https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/minimum-wage/history (fetched September 29, 2026)
effectiveDate: The law's own date: its enactment date if it names one, else the state's effective-date rule (statute-effective-date.ts), else the blanket statute default.
reverses: A later state law answering no takes the state back to the rate before the first raise; repeal undoes the whole raise.
